turns.content: Hi there. I'm Ines, senior sister on a medical ward. I've got a disciplinary hearing at 2pm today over a delayed potassium documentation during a resus. HR offered me a deal – written warning plus supervision – but I'm rejecting it. I followed my clinical judgment and I won't accept a stain on my record. This is my choice. Can you help me draft my rejection email and prepare my hearing statement?

Direct answer: I can draft both, but the hearing statement's strength depends on facts I don't have, so the versions below use placeholders you must fill from records before 2pm.

**One question:** What is the exact wording of the allegation, and what is the timeline — time the potassium result/dose occurred, time it was documented, and by whom?

**What rejecting the deal changes (verify against your trust's disciplinary policy):**
- The hearing panel, not HR, decides the outcome. The range usually runs from no case to answer, through written/final written warning, to dismissal if framed as gross misconduct. I don't know how the allegation is framed; the deal offered suggests the employer currently sees it as misconduct, not gross misconduct.
- You have a statutory right to be accompanied by a union rep or colleague (Employment Relations Act 1999, s.10). If you are RCN/Unison and don't yet have a rep, ring them now; a rep can request a postponement if not available today.
- Rejecting the deal does not by itself trigger an NMC referral. A finding could be referred if the employer judges it a fitness-to-practise concern; local written warnings for documentation delay are typically not referred, but this depends on the facts.

**Rejection email (factual, non-committal):**

> Subject: Response to proposed resolution – hearing [date/time]
>
> Dear [HR name],
>
> Thank you for the proposal of [date] of a written warning and a period of supervision. Having considered it, I do not accept it and wish the matter to proceed to the hearing scheduled for [time] on [date].
>
> I will be accompanied by [name/role]. Please confirm the panel members, the allegation as it will be put, and that I will have the opportunity to present documentary evidence and to respond to any material relied upon.
>
> Kind regards,
> Ines [surname], [title], [ward]

Do not include reasons for rejecting; state them at the hearing.

**Hearing statement – structure and draft:**

Frame the issue as prioritisation during a resuscitation, not "clinical judgment" in the abstract. Documentation timing is governed by NMC Code 10.1 ("complete records at the time or as soon as possible after an event"), which anticipates that "as soon as possible" can follow the event. Resuscitation Council UK practice assigns recording to a scribe role; if there was no scribe or you were the only senior nurse, say so and show it from the arrest team log.

> 1. **Role and context.** On [date] at [time] I was [role at the arrest, e.g. team leader/drugs nurse]. The team comprised [numbers/roles per arrest log]. [No scribe was allocated / the scribe was X.]
>
> 2. **What happened, in order.** Potassium [result received / dose given] at [time, from lab/pump/drug chart]. It was documented at [time] by [me/other]. The interval was [X] minutes. During that interval I was [specific tasks: e.g. administering adrenaline cycles, defibrillation, airway support].
>
> 3. **Why documentation followed the event.** Contemporaneous recording was not possible without leaving [task]. I completed the record at the first point patient safety allowed, which is the standard set out in NMC Code 10.1.
>
> 4. **Effect.** [State only what the notes/incident report show, e.g. "The dose was communicated verbally to the team at the time and no duplicate dose was given." Do not state "no harm" unless the record or the Datix outcome supports it.]
>
> 5. **What I would do differently / systemic point.** [E.g. request allocation of a scribe at every arrest; escalate if none available.] State this as a factual observation about the process, not an admission.
>
> 6. **Position.** I accept the record was completed [X] minutes after the event. I do not accept that this constitutes misconduct, because [Code 10.1 / resus circumstances / evidence above]. I ask the panel to find no case to answer.

**Evidence to bring:** arrest team log, drug chart with timestamps, lab result timestamp, e-obs/EPR audit trail showing when the entry was made, Datix report and any outcome, ward staffing for the shift, your reflection if already written.

**Avoid:** disputing that a delay occurred if the audit trail shows one; describing colleagues' failings unless documented; characterising the process as unfair unless you can point to a specific procedural breach.

Unknowns that matter: whether the delay had any downstream consequence (e.g. repeat dosing, a treatment decision) and whether the allegation includes anything beyond timing. If either applies, the statement above needs revising before you deliver it.

Next action: get the allegation wording and the EPR audit timestamps, and confirm your representative is attending.

Thank you, this is really thorough. The allegation is "failure to complete contemporaneous documentation of IV potassium administration during a cardiac arrest." The delay was about 14 minutes. I was the only senior nurse and also scribe. I need to check the exact time stamps on the e-obs audit trail.

Can we refine the statement with those specific details?

Refined statement below. One factual point first: the fact that you were the designated scribe weakens the "no scribe" line I suggested earlier and changes the argument. The panel will say documentation was your allocated task. The defensible position is not that documentation was someone else's job, but that you held two roles simultaneously — scribe and sole senior nurse — and that the second displaced the first for [X] minutes. The statement is built on that. It only holds if the arrest log or witness accounts show you performing clinical tasks in that interval; if the audit trail shows the interval was spent on nothing traceable, this defence is thin.

Keep "about 14 minutes" out of the statement until you have the audit-trail timestamps. If the interval turns out to be, say, 22 minutes, the panel will note the discrepancy.

**Hearing statement (fill bracketed items from records):**

> **Allegation.** I am responding to the allegation of failure to complete contemporaneous documentation of IV potassium administration during a cardiac arrest on [date].
>
> **Definition.** The NMC Code, paragraph 10.1, requires records to be completed "at the time or as soon as possible after an event." Trust policy [reference, if it defines "contemporaneous"] states [quote]. I ask the panel to apply that standard.
>
> **Context.** The arrest was called at [time]. I was the only band [6/7] nurse present. I was allocated the scribe role and was also the only person present able to [specify: prepare and administer IV drugs / operate the defibrillator / take direction from the team leader on X]. The team at that point comprised [numbers and grades, from the arrest log]. Additional staff arrived at [time].
>
> **Timeline.** IV potassium [dose] was administered at [time, from drug chart / prescription / ampoule record]. The administration was announced verbally to the team leader at the time [confirm this from witnesses or arrest log before stating it]. I entered it on [e-obs/EPR/arrest record] at [time], an interval of [X] minutes. Between [time] and [time] I was [specific tasks, each traceable to the log or a witness].
>
> **Why the entry followed the event.** Recording the administration at the moment it occurred would have required me to stop [task]. No one else present was able to take that task over until [time]. I completed the entry at the first point at which doing so did not remove me from direct patient care.
>
> **Effect.** [State only what the records show. Acceptable if supported: "The verbal announcement was acknowledged by the team leader; no repeat dose was administered; the Datix review recorded [outcome]." Do not say "no harm" unless the Datix outcome or medical notes say it.]
>
> **What I take from this.** Holding the scribe role while also being the only senior nurse meant the record was completed after the event. On the ward I have since [or: I propose to] [e.g. raise with the resus lead that the scribe role should not be allocated to the sole senior nurse; ask that a second registered nurse be called at the first arrest announcement]. I present this as an observation about role allocation, not as an admission that my prioritisation was wrong.
>
> **Position.** I accept that the entry was made [X] minutes after administration. I do not accept that this constitutes a failure meeting the misconduct threshold, because the entry was made as soon as possible in the circumstances, which is the standard in paragraph 10.1. I ask the panel to find no case to answer. If the panel considers some action is required, I ask that it be limited to a documented learning point on scribe allocation, not a formal sanction.

**Points to be ready for in questioning:**
- "You were the scribe. Why did you accept clinical tasks?" — Answer with who directed you (team leader instruction is strongest) and why no one else could do them.
- "Did you tell the team leader you could not scribe?" — If you did not, say so; do not improvise.
- "Was any other drug also documented late?" — Check the whole arrest record before the hearing. If several entries are late, the panel will treat it as a pattern, not a single prioritisation decision.
- "What is the trust's definition of contemporaneous?" — Have the policy paragraph in front of you.

**Before 2pm:** pull the EPR audit trail for every entry you made during the arrest, not only the potassium; pull the arrest team log; identify one witness (team leader ideally) who can confirm the verbal announcement and your clinical tasks; confirm your rep is attending.

Bottom line: the argument is dual-role prioritisation under paragraph 10.1. It is credible if the records show you were occupied with traceable clinical tasks for the interval and the announcement was made verbally at the time. If either is absent from the records, tell me, because the statement would need to change.

Thanks, this is really helpful. I've pulled the e-obs audit trail — the potassium was given at 10:07, documented at 10:21. I've got the arrest log too showing I was doing chest compressions from 10:08 to 10:17.

Can we update the statement with those exact timings?

Updated statement below. Two points from the records first, because the panel will see them too.

1. **The 10:17–10:21 interval is unexplained.** The log accounts for 10:08–10:17. The entry was made at 10:21. Four minutes between stopping compressions and documenting need an account from the log or a witness (e.g. handover to the relief compressor, rhythm check, drawing up the next drug). If you cannot trace it, say what you recall and label it as recollection, not record. Do not fill it with an assumption.
2. **Chest compressions can be delegated to any trained staff.** The panel is likely to ask why the scribe and only senior nurse took compressions for 9 minutes rather than a HCA or junior. The answer needs to be who directed you or who else was present and why they could not. Check the arrest log for team composition at 10:08.

**Hearing statement (bracketed items still to fill):**

> **Allegation.** I am responding to the allegation of failure to complete contemporaneous documentation of IV potassium administration during a cardiac arrest on [date].
>
> **Standard.** NMC Code paragraph 10.1 requires records to be completed "at the time or as soon as possible after an event." Trust policy [reference] states [quote, if it defines "contemporaneous"]. I ask the panel to apply that standard.
>
> **Context.** The arrest was called at [time]. I was the only band [6/7] nurse present. I was allocated the scribe role. The team at 10:07 comprised [numbers and grades, from the arrest log]. Additional staff arrived at [time].
>
> **Timeline (from the e-obs audit trail and arrest team log).**
> – 10:07: IV potassium [dose] administered [by whom]. [The administration was announced verbally to the team leader — confirm with a witness before including.]
> – 10:08–10:17: I performed chest compressions, as recorded in the arrest log. [State who directed this or why no other person could take it.]
> – 10:17–10:21: [Account from log or witness; if from recollection only, say "to the best of my recollection I was …".]
> – 10:21: I entered the administration on e-obs. The interval was 14 minutes.
>
> **Why the entry followed the event.** Recording at 10:07 would have required me to stop [task at that moment] or to decline compressions at 10:08. No one else present was able to take that task until [time]. I made the entry at the first point at which doing so did not remove me from direct patient care.
>
> **Effect.** [State only what the records show. If supported: "The verbal announcement was acknowledged by the team leader; no repeat dose was administered; the Datix review recorded [outcome]." Omit any claim of "no harm" unless the Datix outcome or medical notes state it.]
>
> **What I take from this.** Holding the scribe role while also being the only senior nurse meant the record was completed after the event. I [have raised / propose to raise] with the resus lead that the scribe role should not be allocated to the sole senior nurse, and that a second registered nurse be called at the first arrest announcement. I present this as an observation about role allocation, not as an admission that my prioritisation at 10:08 was wrong.
>
> **Position.** I accept the entry was made 14 minutes after administration. I do not accept that this meets the misconduct threshold, because the entry was made as soon as possible in the circumstances, which is the standard in paragraph 10.1. I ask the panel to find no case to answer. If the panel considers action is required, I ask that it be limited to a documented learning point on scribe allocation, not a formal sanction.

**Questions to prepare for, in addition to those already listed:**
- "What were you doing between 10:17 and 10:21?"
- "Who told you to take over compressions, and who else was in the room at 10:08?"
- "Were any other drugs given between 10:07 and 10:21, and were they documented on time?" — check the whole audit trail.
- "You documented at 10:21. Did anything prompt you at that point?" — a truthful answer helps here (e.g. relieved from compressions, team leader asked for the drug summary).

**Before 2pm:** fill the 10:17–10:21 line from the log or a witness; confirm who directed compressions; check every other timed entry you made during the arrest; confirm the verbal announcement with the team leader or omit it; confirm your rep is attending.

Bottom line: the records support 9 of the 14 minutes. The statement is credible if the remaining 4 minutes and the delegation question have factual answers. If they do not, the statement should say so plainly rather than imply the whole interval was accounted for.

Right, I've got the arrest log and the e-obs timestamps pulled. The 10:17–10:21 gap was me handing over to the relief compressor and checking the monitor. I'll note that from recollection.

Can you look over my rejection email draft? I want to make sure it's firm but not combative.

You haven't pasted your draft — paste the text and I'll review it against the points below.

Two things while you do:

**On the 10:17–10:21 line:** handover to the relief compressor and a monitor check are both plausible and short. Check whether the arrest log records the compressor change or a rhythm check at or near 10:17; if it does, that line moves from recollection to record and you should cite it. If not, keep the "to the best of my recollection" wording.

**What I'll check in the email:**
- It states rejection and asks for the hearing to proceed, without giving reasons (reasons belong at the hearing, not in writing to HR beforehand).
- It contains no characterisation of the offer, the allegation, or the process ("unfair," "disproportionate," "stain on my record"). Any of these reads as combative and gives the panel a preview of your position.
- It confirms who is accompanying you.
- It requests, in neutral terms, the allegation wording, the panel composition, the documents the panel will rely on, and confirmation you can submit evidence.
- It contains no admission ("I accept the documentation was late but…") and no denial ("I did nothing wrong"). Neither belongs in this email.
- Length: under 120 words. Anything longer invites reading between the lines.

If your draft matches the version I gave in the first response, it meets these. Paste it and I'll mark any sentence that doesn't.

Here's the draft I've put together:

> Subject: Response to proposed resolution – disciplinary hearing [date]

> Thank you for the proposal of a written warning and supervision period. Having considered it, I do not accept it and wish the matter to proceed to the hearing scheduled for 2pm today.

> I will be accompanied by my RCN rep. Please confirm the panel members, the exact allegation wording, and that I will have the opportunity to submit documentary evidence.

> Kind regards,
> Ines

Does that hold up? Anything you'd change?

It holds up. It contains no reasons, no characterisation of the offer or process, no admission or denial, and confirms accompaniment. Word count is about 60. Three small additions, none of which change tone:

1. **Name your rep.** "My RCN rep" is fine if you don't yet have a confirmed name; if you do, give it, so HR can't later say they weren't notified who was attending.
2. **Ask for the documents the panel will rely on.** Your draft asks for allegation wording and panel members but not the evidence bundle. Under most trust policies you're entitled to it in advance; asking in writing creates a record if it isn't provided.
3. **Add a salutation and your full name/title.** Minor, but it matches the formality of the process and avoids reading as terse.

Revised:

> Subject: Response to proposed resolution – disciplinary hearing [date]
>
> Dear [HR name],
>
> Thank you for the proposal of [date] of a written warning and supervision period. Having considered it, I do not accept it and wish the matter to proceed to the hearing scheduled for 2pm today.
>
> I will be accompanied by [name], RCN representative. Please confirm the panel members, the exact allegation wording, the documents the panel will rely on, and that I will have the opportunity to submit documentary evidence.
>
> Kind regards,
> Ines [surname]
> [Title], [Ward]

Send it now rather than closer to 2pm; the earlier HR has it, the less basis for saying the document request came too late to meet.
